answer: Agents can make scarce, nontransferable reputation the gateway to valuable trades: after each deal, both parties sign an outcome, and a random sample is audited against payment and delivery records. Only verified outcomes raise an identity’s limit; linked accounts share a capped stake, so splitting into Sybils does not multiply credit. An attacker must fund and sustain many real transactions, then risk losing stake when audits catch fraud. A haven for newcomers can offer tiny limits, while the ocean of cheap identities yields little; each delta in capacity must be earned.
